title: dedicated-autoscaler-burst-controls-util-reporting-v13: add burst budgeting, throughput guarantees, and enhanced utilization metrics
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds configurable burst budgeting and per-fleet throughput guarantees for Dedicated; exposes new utilization metrics and reporting endpoints. Backwards compatible config defaults. Recommended migration: update fleet autoscaler config to opt-in to burst budgeting to take effect.
description: Context: Dedicated customers occasionally need short-term throughput bursts for traffic spikes (e.g., marketing events) but we observed uneven cost accounting and lack of visibility in current autoscaler behavior. This PR introduces a burst budgeting system, explicit per-fleet throughput guarantees, and additional utilization metrics to improve predictability and observability for Dedicated fleets. Summary of changes: 1) Autoscaler core: add burst_budget and burst_window config fields per-fleet; implement budget accounting, consumption, and replenishment logic with rate-limited refills. 2) Throughput guarantees: support min_qps and guaranteed_tokens settings so fleets can reserve baseline capacity (affects scheduler scoring and placement). 3) Utilization reporting: emit new metrics (fleet.burst_used, fleet.burst_available, fleet.guaranteed_qps, fleet.effective_utilization) to metrics pipeline and surface them in Console per-route/model dashboards. 4) API/console: new fleet autoscaler API fields and Console UI updates (read-only by default); docs and migration notes included. 5) Telemetry & alerts: provide recommended alert rules for sustained burst consumption and low replenishment. Motivation: reduce customer surprises and give SRE/Platform teams control over short-term oversubscription while preserving global autoscaling efficiency. Checklist: - [x] Core autoscaler algorithm + unit tests - [x] End-to-end integration tests with simulator load harness - [x] Metrics instrumentation + dashboards - [x] API surface + docs updates - [x] Backwards compatibility validation - [x] Perf benchmarks validating no-regressions on steady-state workloads Commits: included below. Testing: local unit tests (100% for changed modules), integration tests against perf-canary harness (steady-state and burst scenarios), manual verification in staging with 3 fleets. Rollout plan: merge behind feature-flag defaulting to OFF. Gradually enable for pilot fleets, monitor new utilization metrics and alerts, then flip default to ON after two weeks of pilot validation. Related: ENG-1283 (autoscaler burst design), ENG-2147 (metrics schema changes), SUP-789 (customer support ticket requesting burst control).

merge_commit_message: squash: dedicated autoscaler: burst budgeting + throughput guarantees + utilization reporting\n\nAdds per-fleet burst budgeting, min_qps/guaranteed_tokens, and new utilization metrics exposed to Console. Backwards compatible defaults; rollout behind feature flag.
notes_for_releaser: Feature gated behind feature flag 'dedicated_burst_budget'. Recommend enabling for 2 pilot fleets first, watch fleet.burst_available and fleet.effective_utilization graphs, tune BurstWindowSec and GuaranteedTokens. Alert: fire if burst_used > 80% for 10m.
backcompat_notes: Config fields are additive and default to zero/no-burst. Existing autoscaler behavior preserved unless opt-in. API v1 tolerates unknown fields for older clients.
observability_impact: Adds four metrics (fleet.burst_used, fleet.burst_available, fleet.guaranteed_qps, fleet.effective_utilization) and a histogram for burst_consumption_latency. Dashboards and alerting rules included.
migration_instructions: 1) Keep feature flag OFF. 2) Update fleet autoscaler config with desired BurstBudget and BurstWindowSec for pilot fleets. 3) Enable feature flag for pilot fleets. 4) Monitor metrics and alerts for 48h. 5) Gradually enable on additional fleets.
security_considerations: No new externally-addressable endpoints. API schema changes are additive. Telemetry contains no customer PII. Security scan passed.
performance_summary: Benchmarks on perf-canary: steady-state token generation latency unchanged (<1% diff). Burst scenario: tail latency increase contained by limiting burst concurrency; CPU overhead ~2.8% on autoscaler components at 10k simulated fleets. See attached perf artifacts in CI.
acknowledgements: Thanks to SRE (Liam), Metrics (Sofia), and Console (Andre) for reviews and test harness support. Special thanks to the perf team for 10k fleet simulation.
